This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Gangappa S/o Thimmaiah, in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 18.11.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., the deceased Sri.
Gangappa was travelling on his motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-06-EW-3927, near Silk Office, Gowribidanur - Hidugur road, Karekallahalli village, Gowribidanur Taluk, for the purpose of selling flowers.

At that time, the driver of the car bearing registration No. KA-40-AC-6062 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle"), came at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
3. Due to the impact of the collision, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
He was immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Gowribidanur, for first aid.
On medical advice, he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, and thereafter to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, for intensive treatment.
However, despite best medical efforts, the deceased succumbed to the injuries on 19.11.2023 at about 6.40 p.m.
Post-mortem examination was conducted, and thereafter, the body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed the last rites.
The petitioners submit that they incurred expenses of about Rs. 2,00,000/- towards transportation, funeral, and obsequies.
It is further submitted that the accident and resultant death of Sri. Gangappa occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged 53 years, working as a flower vendor and earning a monthly income of about Rs.30,000/-.
4. The petitioners contend that they were entirely dependent on the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: Petitioner No. 1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No. 2 is his daughter, and Petitioner No. 3 is his mother.
On account of his untimely death, they have suffered mental shock, agony, emotional trauma, and loss of breadwinner as well as moral support.

Hence, the petitioners have prayed for award of compensation of Rs. 30,00,000/- with interest, jointly and severally, from Respondent No.
1 - the owner of the offending vehicle, and Respondent No. 2 - the insurer.
5. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and filed their written statements respectively.

6. Respondent No. 1, the RC owner of the offending vehicle, has filed his written statement admitting that he is the registered owner of the car bearing registration No. KA-40-AC-6062 and further admitting that the vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No. 2 under a valid and effective insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
However, he has specifically denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the said vehicle.

It is his assertion that the driver of the car was holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident and that the accident was in fact caused solely due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
On these grounds, Respondent No. 1 has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. Respondent No. 2, the insurer of the offending vehicle, has filed its objection statement.
It has admitted the issuance of a commercial passenger vehicle insurance policy in favour of the offending car and its validity as on the date of the accident.

However, it has contended that its liability, if any,
is subject to the terms, conditions and limitations of the said policy.

Respondent No. 2 has further specifically disputed the age, avocation and income of the deceased, as well as the validity of the permit and fitness certificate of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
It has also denied the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased and the claim of dependency as set up in the petition.
On these grounds, Respondent No. 2 has also prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Gangappa S/o Thimmaiah died due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA- 40-AC-6962 on 18-11-2023 at about 6.45 p.m., near Silk Office, Gowribidanur - Hidugur Road,
Karekallahalli Village, Gowribidanur Taluk?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

if so, what amount?
3.
What order or award ?
9. In support of their claim, Petitioner No.2 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
On the other hand the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

10. Having heard the counsel for both sides and have perused the material on record.

sentences.text:
By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : Partly In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1:- Petitioner No. 2, the daughter of the deceased, entered the witness box as PW1 by filing her affidavit under Order XVIII Rule 4 of CPC in lieu of examination-in-chief.

She has reiterated the averments of the petition, stating that on 18.11.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., the deceased Sri. Gangappa was travelling on his motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-06-EW-3927, near Silk Office, Gowribidanur - Hidugur road, Karekallahalli village, Gowribidanur Taluk, for the purpose of selling flowers, at that time, the driver of the offending car came at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased, causing him fatal injuries.
13. In support of her testimony, PW1 has produced contemporaneous police records.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered on the basis of her first information statement(EX P2).
Exhibits P 4 is the Spot Mahazar and Exhibit P5 is the rough sketch prepared by the investigating officer, which corroborate the manner and place of the accident.
Exhibit P8 is the IMV report showing the damages sustained by the vehicles involved.
Exhibit P3 is the charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer, which squarely fixes responsibility for the accident on the driver of the offending car.

14. During the course of cross-examination, it was suggested by learned counsel for Respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself, inasmuch as he was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.
It was also suggested that the accident was a self-accident and not due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car.
PW1 has categorically denied all such suggestions.
Except for these suggestions, nothing material was elicited in her cross-examination to discredit her version of events.
15. Significantly, no credible evidence was adduced by the respondents to substantiate their plea.
No independent witnesses were examined.

More importantly, if indeed the accident had occurred due to negligence of the deceased, the respondents ought to have examined the driver of the offending car, or produced contrary investigation records, or taken appropriate legal steps to challenge the charge sheet filed by the police.
No such steps were taken.
Thus, the plea of the respondents remains a mere bald allegation, unsupported by any material evidence.

16. It is a well-settled principle that in motor accident claim proceedings, the standard of proof is not that of "beyond reasonable doubt" as in criminal trials, but of "preponderance of probability."

Applying this standard, the oral testimony of PW1, coupled with the contemporaneous police records such as FIR, FIS, Spot Mahazar, sketch, IMV report and charge sheet, collectively establish that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, I hold that the petitioner has successfully proved Issue No. 1, and the same is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: The Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Gangappa.
The Petitioners are the wife, daughter and mother of the deceased.

They have produced the Aadhaar cards of petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.9 to 12, which clearly indicate that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 is the daughter and Petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased.

Hence,
all the Petitioners are considered as LRs and dependents and are entitled for compensation.
18. The petitioners have stated in their claim petition that the deceased was aged 53 years at the time of the accident.
However, on careful scrutiny of the records and evidence produced, it is evident that the petitioners have not been able to substantiate this claim with any cogent material.
19. Ex.P11, the Aadhaar card of the deceased, clearly mentions his date of birth as 15-06-1950.
If this date of birth is taken into consideration, the deceased was aged 73 years as on the date of the accident i.e., 18.11.2023.

Further, Ex. P6, the Inquest Report, and Ex. P7, the Post-Mortem Report,
both prepared by official authorities in the course of investigation, have also recorded the age of the deceased as around 70 years.
20. On the other hand, though the petitioners have pleaded that the deceased was 53 years, they have not produced any documentary evidence to corroborate this assertion.
During the course of cross- examination, PW1, the daughter of the deceased, specifically admitted that as per the Aadhaar card, the date of birth of the deceased is 15-06-1950.

21. It is also to be noted that the Inquest Report, the Post-Mortem Report, and the Aadhaar card, are consistent with one another and mutually corroborate the fact that the deceased was more that 70 years at the time of his death.
These official records are reliable pieces of evidence and carry greater probative value than the bare assertion of the petitioners.
In view of the above, this Tribunal is constrained to hold that the claim of the petitioners regarding the deceased being 53 years old cannot be accepted.
The available documentary evidence and the admission of PW1 establish that the deceased was aged 73 years at the time of the accident.
Accordingly, the age of the deceased is taken as 73 years for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
22. The petitioner claimed that the deceased Gangappa was working as a flower vendor and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The Petitioners are financial and emotionally dependents on the deceased.
Due to his untimely death, they have suffered immense mental shock, agony and loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.
To substantiate the income and avocation of the deceased, the Petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, notional income Rs.16,000/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.
23. As the deceased was aged about 73 years, no future prospects is added on the income of the deceased as per Pranay Sethi case.

As there are 3 dependents, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (Rs.16,000 - 5,333/- =Rs.10,667) (Rs.10,667 X 12) Rs.1,28,004/- and applying 5 multiplier
, Petitioners are awarded Rs.6,40,020/- towards loss of dependency.

sentences.text: 24. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled Rs.44,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost her father and Petitioner No.3 has lost her son.

sentences.text: Total Rs.1,32,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium.
25. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost her father and Petitioner No.3 has lost her son.
Hence, Rs.20,000/- towards loss to estate.

26. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses: Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award Rs.16,500/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.

27. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Amount  Compensation 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,40,020/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
 to Petitioners 3. Loss to estate Rs. 20,000/-
4. Transportation of Rs. 16,500/-
 dead body, Funeral &
 obsequies Expenses
Total Rs
28. Liability
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of rider of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners are awarded compensation of .8,08,520/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.

, Petitioners are awarded Rs.6,40,020/- towards loss of dependency.
24. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
Total Rs.1,32,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium.
25. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost her father and Petitioner No.3 has lost her son.
Hence, Rs.20,000/- towards loss to estate.

26. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses: Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award Rs.16,500/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.

28. Liability
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners are awarded compensation of .8,08,520/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.

After deposit of amount, 50% of the amount is apportioned to 1st Petitioner and 40%
is apportioned to the Petitioner No.2 and 10% is apportioned to the petitioner No.3.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1 and 2, 25% each of the amount shall be kept in FD in their name in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 2 years and balance 75% each amount shall be disbursed to them through E-payment on proper identification.
The entire apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.3 shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
